items.fromString:
h3. Why

With holds now placed in the reservation store at add-to-cart (CORE-18632), the stock count in the inventory database is only decremented after payment capture. Losing that commit is the hardest failure of Checkout V2: the order ships, the shelf count stays high, and the next customer buys an item that is not there.

h3. Scope

* New worker {{shop-worker/src/inventory_sync}} (TypeScript, Node 24, Vitest).
* Trigger: the payments webhook handler (v2, v3 and the expiry path) produces an {{InventorySyncCommand}} on Kafka once the payment is captured or the hold expires.
* On capture: decrement the stock in Postgres in one transaction keyed by {{order_id}}, then emit {{InventorySynced}} and release the hold in Redis.
* On expiry or refund before shipping: release the hold only; the stock count is never touched.
* A nightly reconcile job lists holds older than 24 h with no matching order and releases them.
* Guest carts that never reach checkout are never synced.

h3. Dependencies

* SHOP-3537 (reservation store) and SHOP-3543 (Kafka topics, Redis streams) must land first.
* SHOP-3559 defines the InventorySyncCommand and InventorySynced messages.

content.text: Fault injection (worker killed mid-commit, InventorySynced lost, Postgres unavailable for 10 minutes) loses no stock update and decrements no item twice.
A hold is released only after the stock commit is confirmed, or when the payment expires or is refunded.
Guest carts that never reach checkout are never synced.
The reconcile job reports and releases holds left over for more than 24 hours.
